#### Getting Started

# Grok Build

Grok Build is a coding agent for the terminal. Use it as an interactive TUI, headlessly in scripts or bots, or through the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) in other apps.

## Install

Run the command for your system. It downloads the latest stable release and adds `grok` to your `PATH`:

```bash customLanguage="bashMacLinux"
curl -fsSL https://x.ai/cli/install.sh | bash
```

```bash customLanguage="powershell"
irm https://x.ai/cli/install.ps1 | iex
```

## Run Grok

Start Grok in your project folder:

```bash customLanguage="bash"
cd your-project
grok
```

If your shell can't find `grok`, open a new terminal.

On first launch, Grok opens your browser to sign in, and keeps you signed in after that. If there is no browser, use another method:

| Where you're working | Sign in with | Command |
| -------------------- | ------------ | ------- |
| Your own machine | Browser | `grok` |
| SSH or a remote machine | Device code | `grok login --device-auth` |
| CI and scripts | API key | `export XAI_API_KEY="xai-..."` |

For every sign-in option, see [Authentication](/build/enterprise#authentication).

## Ask your first question

At the prompt, start with a question that works in any repository:

```text
Explain this repo.
```

Grok reads the files it needs, shows each step as it runs, and answers with a summary of the codebase. Once you see that, the install, sign-in and project are all working.

Then point it at a file with `@`:

```text
@src/main.rs Walk me through this file.
```

In a session, `/usage` shows your credit usage.

## Run headlessly

Headless mode is ideal for scripts, automations, or integration into other apps:

```bash customLanguage="bash"
grok -p "Explain this codebase"
grok -p "Explain the architecture" --output-format streaming-json
```

For its flags and output formats, see [Headless and Scripting](/build/cli/headless-scripting).

## Update

One command updates Grok for both interactive and headless use:

```bash customLanguage="bash"
grok update
```

To see what each release changed, read the [Changelog](https://x.ai/changelog/build).

## Requirements

* macOS (Apple silicon or Intel) or Linux (x86\_64 or arm64). On Windows, use PowerShell, Git Bash or WSL.
* A terminal, and a project folder to run Grok in.
* A SpaceXSI account to sign in with, or an API key.

## Features

* [Plugins, skills](/build/features/skills-plugins-marketplaces) and [MCP servers](/build/features/mcp-servers). Extend what Grok can do.
* [Agent Dashboard](/build/features/dashboard). Every session at a glance, and which agents need input.
* [Modes and Commands](/build/modes-and-commands). Switch modes with Shift+Tab and use slash commands.
* [CLI Reference](/build/cli/reference). The `grok` subcommands and common flags.

## Next

* [Custom Models](/build/settings/reference#modelid). Use any model through `~/.grok/config.toml`.
* [Grok 4.7 on the API](/developers/grok-4-7#using-the-api). Call the model from your own agent or tool.
* [Enterprise Deployments](/build/enterprise)
* [Grok Bot](/grok-bot/overview) — AI teammates on a cloud computer

# Settings

Grok Build offers a variety of configurations to suit your needs, many of which are made directly available in the TUI under `/settings`.

Settings are persisted under `~/.grok/config.toml` (on Windows, `%USERPROFILE%\.grok\config.toml`). To configure the default home directory, you can set `$GROK_HOME`.

For MCP servers, see [MCP Servers](/build/features/mcp-servers). For marketplaces, skills, and plugins, see [Skills, Plugins, and Marketplaces](/build/features/skills-plugins-marketplaces); for hooks, see [Hooks](/build/features/hooks).

## Scopes

| Scope | Path | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Environment | `GROK_*` (and related) variables | Session / CI overrides |
| User | `~/.grok/config.toml` (or `$GROK_HOME/config.toml`) | Personal defaults |
| Project | `.grok/config.toml` in the repo | Repo-shared MCP, plugins, and permission rules |
| Managed | `~/.grok/managed_config.toml`, `/etc/grok/managed_config.toml` | Enterprise-served defaults |
| Requirements | `~/.grok/requirements.toml`, `/etc/grok/requirements.toml` | Policy pins |

Project configs are limited to MCP servers, plugins, and permission rules, not full user configs. For scope merge order and managed deployments, see [Enterprise Deployments](/build/enterprise#configuration). Day-to-day [permissions](/build/features/permissions) and [sandbox](/build/features/sandbox) apply to individual use; managed locks and headless modes are under Enterprise.

## Verification

To confirm which configs are picked up by Grok Build, run the following command:

```bash customLanguage="bash"
grok inspect
```

## Example `config.toml`

Copy into `$GROK_HOME/config.toml`, or `~/.grok/config.toml` when `GROK_HOME` is unset. Prefer `/settings` for UI, notifications, and other in-app options.

```toml customLanguage="toml"
[models]
default = "grok-build"                       # recommended for coding / agent sessions
web_search = "grok-4.7"                      # model used by client-side web_search tool

[model."grok-4.7"]
model = "grok-4.7"                           # id sent to the API
base_url = "https://api.x.ai/v1"             # provider endpoint
name = "Grok 4.7"                            # shown in model picker
description = "Grok 4.7 from SpaceXSI"
env_key = "XAI_API_KEY"                      # env var holding the API key
api_backend = "responses"                    # chat_completions | responses | messages
temperature = 0.7
top_p = 0.95
max_completion_tokens = 8192
context_window = 500000
extra_headers = { "x-api-key" = "xai-..." }
supports_backend_search = true               # if the endpoint supports Grok-hosted server-side search tools

[mcp_servers.filesystem]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/path/to/allowed/directory"]
enabled = true
startup_timeout_sec = 30
tool_timeout_sec = 6000

[mcp_servers.linear]
url = "https://mcp.linear.app/mcp"
headers = { "Authorization" = "Bearer ${LINEAR_API_KEY}", "x-mcp-session-id" = "{{session_id}}" }

[ui]
compact_mode = false
theme = "auto"
show_thinking_blocks = true
```

## TOML Values

For a selection of `config.toml` keys, see [TOML Values](/build/settings/reference#toml-values).
